comply-in.span: A clear cost, accuracy, and freshness trade-off analysis for RAG vs long-context windows, grounded in 2026 benchmarks.
A specific architecture choice—RAG hybrid with long-context fallback—with the reasoning behind it, before any build begins.
Small context windows (under 16K tokens) use RAG; large context windows (1M+ tokens) rely on long-context, with a trigger threshold for freshness-based retrievals.
If your project's data is static and under 100K tokens, long-context alone is cheaper and simpler. I'll say so.

sec-head.h2: What is RAG? What is long context?

p: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves external knowledge from a vector database and inserts it into an LLM's context window dynamically. Long-context windows extend the LLM's native memory to accept 100K+ tokens of raw data directly. Both are open patterns by 2026, but RAG remains ~40% cheaper for production at scale, while long-context offers zero retrieval latency and higher accuracy on single-source document Q&A.

sec-head.h2: Architecture comparison: RAG vs Long Context

td: Freshness, cost efficiency, and handling large-scale heterogenous data
Zero retrieval overhead, highest accuracy on static document comprehension
Real-time, multi-source, or frequently updated knowledge bases
Single-document deep analysis, legal contracts, or book summaries

p: Neither wins alone for all cases. The optimal architecture uses RAG as the default retrieval path for real-time and cost-sensitive queries, with a long-context fallback when accuracy on a single document is critical. I build hybrid systems that dynamically switch based on query intent, source count, and freshness requirements.
